name: Modern CSS Reset
one_line: Minimal global reset normalizing margins, box-sizing, and media defaults.
why_pro: Eliminates browser inconsistencies so every project starts from predictable ground zero.
demo_idea: Build a 'before/after' page showing the same unstyled markup with and without a modern reset applied, toggled live.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build an interactive 'before/after' page that toggles a modern CSS reset on identical markup so its effect is instantly visible. TECHNIQUE: a modern CSS reset — `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }`, `* { margin: 0 }`, `img, video { max-width: 100%; display: block }`, and `input, button, textarea, select { font: inherit }`, optionally with `[role='list']` list normalization and `text-size-adjust`. BUILD: (1) Render the same card component (heading, image, list, form) in two side-by-side panes; (2) apply the reset only to the second pane via a scoping class; (3) add toggle buttons that add/remove the reset class live; (4) display the reset snippet in a code block for reference. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Style it on a dark neutral background (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4 text). No feature detection needed — reset CSS degrades gracefully by nature. Verify both panes render identical markup and the toggle flips UA inconsistencies like list margins and baseline images on and off.

name: Attribute Selectors
one_line: Select elements by attribute presence, value, prefix, or substring matches.
why_pro: Targets state and data attributes without adding classes — the backbone of data-attribute styling systems.
demo_idea: Style a mock design-system page where data-variant/data-size attributes drive button, badge, and input looks purely via [attr] selectors.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a mock design-system page where buttons, badges, and inputs are styled purely through attribute selectors, with zero presentational classes. TECHNIQUE: CSS attribute selectors — presence `[data-variant]`, exact match `[data-variant="primary"]`, whitespace-list match `[data-badge~="status"]`, prefix `[href^="https://"]`, suffix `[href$=".pdf"]`, substring `[href*="github"]`, and boolean-state flips like `[data-control][aria-invalid="true"]`. BUILD: (1) Create rows of buttons with data-variant/data-size combos; (2) badge spans using ~= list matching plus a data-state selected ring; (3) inputs where a script toggles aria-invalid to recolor the border live; (4) links styled by href prefix/suffix/substring including a `::after` PDF marker. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Attribute selectors are universally supported, so no fallback needed — but keep markup valid since invalid attributes simply don't match.

name: UI State Pseudo-classes
one_line: :hover, :focus-visible, :active, :disabled, :checked for interactive states.
why_pro: Communicates interactivity and feedback without JavaScript state management.
demo_idea: Create a fully CSS-driven settings panel where :checked toggles switch cards, radio chips, and a live preview theme.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a fully CSS-driven settings panel where checkbox switches, radio chips, a live-preview theme, and button states all respond with zero JavaScript. TECHNIQUE: UI state pseudo-classes — `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:active`, `:disabled`, and especially `:checked` combined with sibling combinators: hide the input with `position:absolute; opacity:0`, then style `.switch input:checked ~ .knob` and `input:checked + label`, and let a radio group recolor a preview via `#t-mint:checked ~ .panel .preview`. BUILD: (1) A visually-hidden checkbox per switch card animating a knob via `::after` transform; (2) radio chips using the adjacent-sibling `+` selector; (3) a preview block themed by named radio inputs; (4) buttons demonstrating :hover/:active/:disabled. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline CSS only, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4). Pseudo-classes are universally supported — no fallback needed — but keep hidden inputs keyboard-accessible so :focus-visible rings still render.

name: CSS Custom Properties
one_line: Cascade-inheriting variables set with --name and read with var().
why_pro: Enables theming, tokens, and component-scoped values that media/container queries can retarget.
demo_idea: Build a color-theme playground: pick hues from swatches that only reassign three custom properties, recoloring the whole page.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a color-theme playground where clicking hue swatches recolors the entire page by reassigning only two or three CSS custom properties. TECHNIQUE: CSS custom properties — define `--hue-accent` and `--hue-bg` on `:root`, derive every color as `hsl(var(--hue-accent), 85%, 68%)`, and override them at runtime with `document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--hue-accent', hue)`. BUILD: (1) Declare the token system in `:root` with hsl() compositions; (2) build cards, buttons, badges, and code text that all read `var()`; (3) add a swatch row where each button sets the two hue variables; (4) show the current `:root` assignment in a live monospace readout. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral base (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4) tinted by the tokens. Custom properties are universally supported — no feature detect needed. Verify the swatch clicks recolor every derived surface, not just the accent, and transitions feel smooth.

name: Cascade Layers (@layer)
one_line: Explicit layer ordering that beats specificity wars in the cascade.
why_pro: Lets teams guarantee reset < base < components < utilities priority without !important.
demo_idea: Demo two stylesheets with clashing class names resolved cleanly by declaring @layer order — show the winner flip as layer order changes.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a live demo where two stylesheets define a clashing class and the winner flips purely by changing @layer declaration order. TECHNIQUE: CSS cascade layers — declare an order with `@layer theme, utilities;`, define rules inside `@layer name { ... }`, and rely on the rule that later layers win regardless of specificity, while unlayered styles beat all layered ones. BUILD: (1) Declare two layers holding different `.callout` styles with identical class specificity; (2) add buttons that rewrite the layer statement via `styleSheets[0].insertRule('@layer utilities, theme;', 0)` so the winner visibly swaps; (3) include a third unlayered `.override` variant that always wins to demonstrate layer precedence; (4) show the current layer order in a code line. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Feature-detect `CSSLayerBlockRule` or `CSS.supports` and show a fallback message on very old browsers; modern evergreen browsers all support @layer.

name: Native CSS Nesting
one_line: Write nested selectors natively without preprocessors.
why_pro: Collocates component styles, cutting build-tool dependencies and selector duplication.
demo_idea: Style a nested card component showing raw nested CSS next to its rendered result, with hover states nested inline.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a side-by-side page showing a card component styled with native CSS nesting next to its actual nested source code. TECHNIQUE: native CSS nesting — write parent rules with inline child blocks using the nesting selector `&`, e.g. `.card { & header { & img { ... } } & footer button { &:hover { ... } } &:hover { border-color: ... } }`. BUILD: (1) Style a social-post card entirely inside one nested block: header, avatar, paragraph, footer buttons with nested :hover; (2) render the exact nested source in a `<pre>` pane beside the live card; (3) feature-detect with `CSS.supports('selector(&)')` and swap in an unstyled-fallback warning message if unsupported. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no preprocessor, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). The demo must genuinely use nested syntax (not flattened selectors) so the source pane and rendered result match one-to-one, letting the reader map each nested block to what they see.

name: Container Queries
one_line: Style elements based on their container's size, not the viewport.
why_pro: Makes true reusable components that adapt to wherever they're placed.
demo_idea: Drop the same card into narrow, medium, and wide containers on one page; the card restyles itself per container via @container.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Drop the identical card component into narrow, medium, and wide containers on one page and have it restyle itself per container with @container queries. TECHNIQUE: container queries — set `container-type: inline-size` on a wrapper, then write `@container (max-width: 259px) { ... }` and `@container (min-width: 260px) { ... }` blocks that change layout, type size, and button shape. BUILD: (1) Build one card (media bar, title, copy, button); (2) place three copies in 200px, 320px, and full-width slots; (3) style the narrow variant stacked and centered, medium horizontal with side media, wide with media on the right and larger type; (4) feature-detect with `CSS.supports('container-type: inline-size')` and show a fallback notice. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries, no viewport media queries for the card itself. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Verify resizing the window changes each card independently of the viewport.

name: Container Query Units (cqi/cqw)
one_line: Size type and spacing relative to container, not viewport (cqi, cqw, cqh).
why_pro: Components scale proportionally inside any slot — fluid design without viewport coupling.
demo_idea: A resizable split pane where headings and padding grow with each pane's own width using cqi units.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a resizable split-pane playground where headings, padding, and badges scale with each pane's own width using container query units. TECHNIQUE: container query units — `1cqi` equals 1% of the container's inline size (also cqw/cqh/cqb), applied as `font-size: 6cqi`, `padding: 4cqi`, with `container-type: inline-size` on the parent. BUILD: (1) Make a `resize: horizontal` dashed container holding a card whose headline is 6cqi, body 3.2cqi, padding 4cqi; (2) add two independent side-by-side containers both using 8cqi type to prove the absolute size differs per container; (3) wire a `ResizeObserver` to display the live container width and the computed pixel size of 6cqi. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Feature-detect with `CSS.supports('font-size: 1cqi')` and fall back to rem-based sizing with a notice if unsupported. Verify dragging edges rescales text smoothly.

name: Relational Selector :has()
one_line: Style parents and ancestors based on their descendants.
why_pro: The 'parent selector' unlocks form validation, conditional layouts, and state styling in pure CSS.
demo_idea: A checkout form where :has(input:invalid) turns the card red, disables the pay button, and reveals hints — no JavaScript.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a checkout form where invalid input turns the card red, disables the pay button, and reveals per-field hints — driven by :has() with essentially no JavaScript. TECHNIQUE: the relational pseudo-class — `form:has(input:invalid)` styles the ancestor based on descendants: flip the border, recolor the submit button, show hidden `.hint` elements; pair with `form:not(:has(input:invalid))` for the success state and `input:invalid`/`input:valid` per-field borders. BUILD: (1) Create card-number, expiry, and CVC inputs with `pattern` attributes and `novalidate` on the form; (2) style `form:has(input:invalid)` for red state plus hint reveal; (3) use one tiny script only to toggle the `disabled` property on submit and feature-detect `CSS.supports('selector(:has(*))')` with a notice. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). All state changes must come from CSS reacting to DOM validity, not classes set by script.

name: Typed Custom Properties (@property)
one_line: Register custom properties with syntax types, defaults, and inheritance.
why_pro: Makes custom properties animatable and type-safe — the key to smooth gradient and counter tricks.
demo_idea: Animate a conic-gradient progress ring by transitioning a registered @property angle value with a range slider.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Animate a conic-gradient progress ring by transitioning a registered @property angle value, driven by a range slider. TECHNIQUE: the @property at-rule — register `@property --angle { syntax: '<angle>'; inherits: false; initial-value: 0deg }`, paint the ring with `background: conic-gradient(#8b7cff var(--angle), #23233a 0)`, and enable `transition: --angle .1s linear` (impossible for untyped custom properties). BUILD: (1) Register the typed property at the top of the stylesheet; (2) build a donut ring using the conic gradient with an inner ::before hole and a centered percentage label; (3) wire a range slider that sets `element.style.setProperty('--angle', p * 3.6 + 'deg')`; (4) add a short auto-fill loop on load to show the transition even without input; (5) feature-detect and show a fallback message if @property is unsupported. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Verify the gradient sweeps smoothly rather than snapping.

name: Style Queries (@container style())
one_line: Query a container's custom-property values, not just its size.
why_pro: Components react to semantic state (data-theme, tone) passed down as variables.
demo_idea: A gallery where each tile reads a --tone variable from its parent and restyles itself, driven by theme chips.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a gallery where each tile restyles itself by reading a --tone custom property from its parent through @container style() queries, driven by theme chips. TECHNIQUE: style queries — a container parent carries `--tone: cool` (set via `element.style.setProperty`), and children write `@container style(--tone: warm) { ... }` blocks that change background, border, and heading color without any class swapping. BUILD: (1) Create a chip row that sets `--tone` on the gallery to warm/cool/fresh; (2) render six identical tiles whose inner card styles react through three `@container style(--tone: ...)` blocks; (3) feature-detect by parsing a style-query rule into a `<style>` sheet and checking rule support, showing a fallback notice on failure. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Note style queries ship behind flags in some engines — the fallback message is mandatory. Verify chip clicks recolor all tiles simultaneously with smooth transitions.

name: Grid Auto-placement & Dense Packing
one_line: Automatic item placement with grid-auto-flow, spans, and dense packing.
why_pro: Fills gaps and builds responsive galleries without measuring or JS masonry.
demo_idea: A photo wall where items of varied span values repack live as you add/remove tiles and toggle dense flow.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a photo wall where tiles of varied span values repack live as items are added, removed, and reshaped, with a toggle for dense auto-placement. TECHNIQUE: CSS Grid auto-placement — `grid-auto-flow: row` vs `row dense`, plus span declarations like `grid-column: span 2` and `grid-row: span 2`; dense mode lets the placement algorithm backfill gaps left by large items. BUILD: (1) Create a `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(110px, 1fr))` wall with fixed 80px auto rows; (2) add buttons to add/remove tiles and a select that sets the next tile's span (1×1, 2×1, 1×2, 2×2); (3) a dense on/off toggle that flips `grid-auto-flow`; (4) make each tile click-removable so holes appear and repack. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text) with bright tile colors. Grid auto-placement is universally supported — no feature detect needed. Verify the dense toggle visibly changes packing when holes exist.

name: Subgrid
one_line: Nested grids inherit parent row/column tracks for cross-item alignment.
why_pro: Aligns card titles, footers, and CTAs across siblings of different content lengths.
demo_idea: A pricing row of three cards with ragged copy where subgrid keeps every heading, list, and button on shared baselines.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a pricing row of three cards with ragged copy lengths where subgrid keeps every name, price, feature list, and button on shared baseline rows. TECHNIQUE: CSS subgrid — the parent grid defines `grid-template-rows` (or columns) and each card uses `grid-row: span 4; grid-template-rows: subgrid` to inherit those tracks instead of creating its own. BUILD: (1) Create a 3-column `.pricing` grid with a 4-row implicit track structure; (2) style each plan as a subgrid card: name row, price row, features row, button row (with `align-self:end` on the button); (3) make the copy lengths deliberately different to prove alignment; (4) feature-detect `CSS.supports('grid-template-rows: subgrid')` and show a fallback notice. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text) with one featured accent card. Verify buttons align on one line regardless of list length, and the layout collapses gracefully on mobile to a single column.

name: Native CSS Masonry
one_line: grid-template-rows/columns: masonry packing items into staggered columns.
why_pro: Pinterest-style layouts natively, no JS measuring or absolute positioning.
demo_idea: A masonry image wall of varied-height cards built with experimental masonry grid, with a toggle to plain grid.

name: CSS Anchor Positioning
one_line: Position popovers/tooltips relative to anchor elements natively.
why_pro: Replaces floating-UI libraries for tooltips, menus, and toasts with platform primitives.
demo_idea: A toolbar with tooltips, dropdown menus, and a color picker popover all anchored via anchor-name/position-anchor, flipping near edges.

name: Scroll-driven Animations (CSS)
one_line: Drive animation progress from scroll position via scroll() and view() timelines.
why_pro: Replaces scroll-listener JS with compositor-smooth, jank-free effects.
demo_idea: A scrollytelling page where a progress bar, image parallax, and rotating 3D cube are pure CSS animation-timeline effects.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a scrollytelling page where a top progress bar, parallax headlines, and a rotating 3D cube are all pure CSS scroll-driven animations. TECHNIQUE: animation-timeline — use scroll(root block) for document-scrubbed effects (progress bar scaleX, cube rotation) and view() with animation-range: entry 0% cover 50% for per-element parallax entrances; keyframes are ordinary @keyframes. BUILD: (1) Fix a progress bar with transform-origin: left animated from scaleX(0) to scaleX(1) on scroll(root block); (2) build three full-height sections whose headings drift and fade via the view() timeline; (3) create a CSS 3D cube (six faces, transform-style: preserve-3d) whose rotation is scrubbed by document scroll; (4) feature-detect CSS.supports('animation-timeline: view()') and show a fallback notice. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries, no scroll JavaScript. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Verify scrolling scrubs all three effects smoothly with zero rAF loops.

name: View Transitions (same-document)
one_line: Animated morphs between DOM states via view-transition-name snapshots.
why_pro: Hollywood-quality state changes with a single API call and CSS control.
demo_idea: A thumbnail grid that expands to a detail page-like view where the clicked image morphs into place via view transitions.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a thumbnail grid that expands to a detail view where the clicked image morphs into place using same-document view transitions. TECHNIQUE: the View Transitions API — call document.startViewTransition(callback), assign a matching view-transition-name: hero to both the clicked thumbnail and the detail hero, and the browser cross-fades and morphs them automatically; style the animation with ::view-transition-old(hero) and ::view-transition-new(hero). BUILD: (1) Create a 3x2 gradient thumbnail grid; (2) a hidden detail view with a 16:9 hero, title, copy, and back button; (3) on click, move the shared vt class to the clicked thumb and swap views inside startViewTransition; (4) on back, reverse the swap; (5) feature-detect document.startViewTransition and fall back to an instant swap. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries, no router. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Verify the clicked tile visibly flies into the hero position and back out.

name: Houdini Paint Worklet
one_line: Register custom paint functions usable as background/image values.
why_pro: Custom textures, borders, and effects impossible in plain CSS, still GPU-composited.
demo_idea: A card set painted with a registered 'confetti' and 'hatching' paint worklet, with input properties driving density live.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a card set whose backgrounds are painted by registered Houdini paint worklets (confetti dots and diagonal hatching) with input properties driving density and angle live. TECHNIQUE: the CSS Painting API — define registerPaint('confetti', class { static get inputProperties() {...} paint(ctx, size, props) {...} }) inside a Blob module URL, register with CSS.paintWorklet.addModule(url), and consume with background-image: paint(confetti) plus custom properties like --confetti-density. BUILD: (1) Write two worklet sources as template strings turned into Blob URLs; (2) paint two cards via the paint() function; (3) sliders that setProperty the density and angle custom properties, triggering instant repaints; (4) feature-detect paintWorklet in CSS and fall back to plain colored backgrounds with a notice. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries, no external worklet files. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Verify slider changes repaint the paint() backgrounds without reload.

name: Logical Properties & Flow-relative Layout
one_line: margin-inline, padding-block, inset-inline — physical axes mapped to writing direction.
why_pro: One stylesheet serves LTR and RTL correctly with zero duplicate rules.
demo_idea: A magazine page with a language toggle (EN/AR) where every margin, border, and float flips logically — no RTL-specific CSS.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a magazine-style page with an EN/AR toggle where every margin, border, float, and size flips direction using only logical properties — zero RTL-specific CSS. TECHNIQUE: CSS logical properties — margin-inline-start, padding-block, border-inline-start, inline-size/block-size, float: inline-start, and text-align: start, all keyed off the dir attribute so RTL flips are automatic. BUILD: (1) Style an article with an inline-start accent border and block margins; (2) a byline row whose avatar gap uses inline spacing; (3) a floating pull-quote block with float: inline-start and inline-end margin; (4) chips spaced with margin-inline-end; (5) two buttons that flip document.documentElement.dir between ltr and rtl and swap the byline text to Arabic. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries, no dir=rtl override rules. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Logical properties are universally supported — verify the border, float, and chip spacing all mirror when toggling to RTL.

name: Fluid Sizing with min()/max()/clamp()
one_line: Bound values between ideals: clamp(min, preferred, max).
why_pro: Fluid, responsive sizing without breakpoint soup or JS.
demo_idea: A hero whose heading, spacing, and image width all breathe smoothly as the window resizes, each labeled with its clamp expression.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a hero section whose heading, padding, media width, and grid gaps all breathe fluidly as the window resizes, each labeled with its live clamp expression. TECHNIQUE: intrinsic sizing functions — clamp(min, preferred, max) for fluid type (font-size: clamp(1.6rem, 5vw, 3.4rem)) and padding, plus max()/min() guards like minmax(min(200px, 100%), 1fr) to prevent overflow. BUILD: (1) Hero with clamped heading, paragraph capped at 65ch, clamped padding, and a clamp(220px, 60%, 480px) media block with aspect-ratio; (2) a grid whose gap is clamped and columns use the min() overflow guard; (3) a readout panel that recomputes each value's actual computed px on resize via getComputedStyle. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries, no media queries for sizing. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). These functions are universally supported — no fallback needed. Verify dragging the window edge moves every readout between its stated bounds.

name: Forgiving Selectors :is() and :where()
one_line: Compact multi-target selectors; :where() adds zero specificity.
why_pro: Shorter stylesheets and safe base styles that easy to override.
demo_idea: A long-form article styled with :where() base typography that any utility class can override — show specificity scores inline.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a long-form article demo where :where() provides zero-specificity base typography that utility classes can override, with specificity scores displayed inline. TECHNIQUE: forgiving selectors — :where(article) :where(h2, p, li) applies styles at (0,0,0) so a single .lead class wins, while :is(section, #featured) p inherits the specificity of its most specific argument (1,0,1) and cannot be outgunned by classes. BUILD: (1) Style an article's h2/p with :where() wrappers as a gray baseline; (2) add .lead and .note-text utility paragraphs that visibly override the baseline; (3) nest a second article under #featured and use :is() to force gold text; (4) render a specificity scoreboard listing each selector and its (a,b,c) score with win/lose markers. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). :is()/:where() are supported in all evergreen browsers — no feature detect needed. Verify utility classes genuinely beat the :where() rules by cascade weight alone.

name: text-wrap: balance & pretty
one_line: Balanced line breaking for headings and ragged text blocks.
why_pro: Kills orphan words and lopsided headlines with one declaration.
demo_idea: Side-by-side headlines and paragraphs with wrap toggled between normal/balance/pretty showing raggedness change.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build a side-by-side comparison page where headlines and paragraphs toggle between text-wrap normal, balance, and pretty, making raggedness differences obvious. TECHNIQUE: text wrapping control — text-wrap: balance evens out line lengths on headlines (limited to about six lines in engines), text-wrap: pretty prevents orphan last words in body copy, versus the default greedy algorithm. BUILD: (1) Create paired boxes: one with a long two-line headline, one with multi-line body copy; (2) three toggle buttons setting a body class (empty, w-balance, w-pretty) that switches the text-wrap value; (3) include a short Ship-it headline to show balance does nothing under three lines and a long headline where it shines; (4) label each box with its monospace property value; (5) feature-detect CSS.supports('text-wrap: balance') with a notice. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Verify toggling visibly reflows lines, especially the headline rag.

name: Scoped Styles (@scope)
one_line: Limit selector reach to a DOM subtree with @scope and proximity weighting.
why_pro: Encapsulated styles without web components or class-name conventions.
demo_idea: Two nested article widgets with identically-named .title classes styled differently via @scope blocks.
agent_prompt: You are a front-end engineer. GOAL: Build two nested article widgets with identically-named .title and .body classes that style differently via @scope blocks, proving encapsulation without naming conventions. TECHNIQUE: the @scope at-rule — @scope (.widget-a) { .title { ... } :scope { ... } } scopes rules to a subtree, where :scope targets the scoping root itself, and @scope (from) to (boundary) supports donut-scoping with proximity resolution. BUILD: (1) Render two widgets with identical inner class names; (2) scope widget-a to violet styling with an italic body and violet border via :scope; (3) scope widget-b to green uppercase styling; (4) explain donut boundaries in a note; (5) feature-detect by parsing a @scope rule into a temporary style element and checking for CSSScopeRule, showing a fallback notice on failure. CONSTRAINTS: one self-contained HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no libraries, no BEM prefixes or shadow DOM. Dark neutral theme (#0d0d0d bg, #e4e4e4 text). Verify both widgets render their own palettes from the same class names.

name: overscroll-behavior & Scroll Containment
one_line: Prevent scroll chaining and pull-to-refresh bleed in nested scrollers.
why_pro: Critical polish for modals, chat panes, and carousels inside scrollable pages.

name: Kinetic Typography
one_line: Words that move, split, and reassemble as an expressive act.
why_pro: Hero moments in campaigns and award-site headers.

Split the headline in JS: wrap each line in a block span with overflow:hidden (the mask) and each word in an inline-block span with class .w. Animate with gsap.fromTo('.w', {yPercent:120, rotation:random, opacity:0}, {yPercent:0, rotation:0, duration:1.1, ease:'elastic.out(1,0.55)', stagger:{each:0.09, from:'random'}}) — the elastic ease makes words spring and settle. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no API keys. Feature-detect window.gsap — if missing, leave the plain headline visible and show fallback text 'GSAP unavailable - static headline shown'. Keep it under 150 lines.

BUILD: (1) dark #0d0d0d centered hero; (2) the counter with clamp() sizing and font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums so digits do not jitter; (3) JS count-up from 0 to 2,481,937 over 2.6 seconds with a quartic ease-out and toLocaleString comma formatting; (4) uppercase letter-spaced label and a hint line. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no API keys. Wrap the clip styles in @supports (background-clip:text) and feature-detect with CSS.supports — if unsupported, fall back to a solid #7ee8fa color and show fallback text 'gradient text clip unsupported'. Under 110 lines.

name: Animate-along-axis Type
one_line: Drive font-variation-settings from scroll, pointer, or audio.
why_pro: Type becomes a living sensor-reactive material.

agent_prompt: You are building variable-font axis animation. GOAL: a headline whose weight leans toward the cursor and whose thickness pulses with an audio tone's amplitude. TECHNIQUE: font-variation-settings driven per frame. Load the variable font Fraunces from the Google Fonts CSS2 API with the wght axis 100..900. On pointermove, compute the normalized distance from the headline center and set el.style.fontVariationSettings = '"wght" W' where W = 900 minus distance times 700, with a 0.08s linear transition for smoothness. For the audio path, use the Web Audio API: create an AudioContext, a 110Hz oscillator feeding an AnalyserNode; in a requestAnimationFrame loop call getByteTimeDomainData, find the peak deviation from 128, and map it into a wght pulse between 300 and 900. BUILD: (1) dark #0d0d0d centered stage with the STRETCH headline; (2) the pointer-weight behavior; (3) a 'Toggle tone' button that starts and stops the oscillator; (4) a status line describing the current mode. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no API keys. Feature-detect document.fonts and AudioContext — if unsupported, keep a static font-weight and show fallback text 'variable axes unsupported - static headline shown'. Under 160 lines.

Under 100 lines.

Under 90 lines.

name: OKLCH Perceptual Color
one_line: Define colors in a perceptually uniform space (L, C, H).
why_pro: Uniform lightness means accessible palettes generated by math, not eyeballing.
demo_idea: A palette generator: pick hue and chroma, watch an even-lightness ramp build in OKLCH with contrast ratios shown per step.
agent_prompt: You are building an OKLCH palette generator. GOAL: an 11-step even-lightness color ramp generated from hue and chroma sliders, with contrast ratios shown per step. TECHNIQUE: the oklch() color function — oklch(L C H) where L is perceptual lightness 0-1, C chroma, H hue in degrees. Because OKLCH is perceptually uniform, stepping L linearly (0.95 down to 0.05) yields visually even tints — the whole point versus HSL. BUILD: (1) dark #0d0d0d layout with two range inputs (hue 0-360, chroma 0-0.32) and a monospace CSS output block printing each step as --step-N: oklch(...); (2) an 11-column grid of swatches; (3) on input, regenerate each swatch with background:oklch(L, C, H), label it with its L value, and show an approximate contrast ratio against white — estimate luminance from L (Y is roughly L cubed) and compute (1.05)/(Y+0.05), clamped 1-21; (4) choose black or white foreground text per swatch by the same luminance. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no API keys. Feature-detect with CSS.supports('color','oklch(50% 0.1 200)') — if unsupported, fall back to an hsl() approximation of the same ramp and show fallback text 'oklch unsupported - hsl approximation shown'. Under 130 lines.

agent_prompt: You are building a color-mix() demo. GOAL: a hover state derived live by mixing toward black in a perceptual space, plus a visual mixer panel. TECHNIQUE: color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand), black 35%) — the percentages say 65% brand, 35% black; oklab keeps the mix perceptually even (no muddy HSL grays). Use it directly in CSS for the button's :hover background with a transition, and use it inline in JS to paint the result swatch. BUILD: (1) dark #0d0d0d page, centered; (2) a mixer row: brand swatch, 'in oklab' label, black swatch, equals sign, result swatch painted with the same color-mix() expression; (3) a monospace formula line showing the exact CSS; (4) a brand-colored button whose hover/focus background is color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand), black 35%) with transition:background 0.35s; (5) a hint explaining that hover states are derived, not hand-picked. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no API keys. Feature-detect with CSS.supports('background','color-mix(in oklab, red, black)') — if unsupported, keep a static darker hover via a predefined hex and show fallback text 'color-mix unsupported'. Under 110 lines.

name: Relative Color Syntax
one_line: Derive new colors from existing ones: oklch(from var(--brand) calc(l*0.9) c h).
why_pro: Programmatic color systems — one brand token generates a whole scale.
demo_idea: A swatch board where one input color fans out into tints, shades, and desaturated variants computed with relative color syntax.
agent_prompt: You are building a relative color syntax demo. GOAL: one brand token fans out into a full scale of tints, shades, and hue-shifted variants computed purely in CSS. TECHNIQUE: relative color syntax — oklch(from var(--brand) calc(l + 0.1) c h) destructures the origin color into l, c, h channels that you can transform with calc(). Build 12 variants: three tints (l + 0.1/0.2/0.3), three shades (l − 0.15/0.3/0.45), two desaturations (calc(c * 0.5) and calc(c * 0.15)), hue rotations (h + 40, h + 120, h − 120), and a complement (h + 180). name: Spring Physics Motion
one_line: Mass/stiffness/damping simulation for organic settle.
why_pro: Springs feel alive — the default of modern design systems' motion.

agent_prompt: You are building a spring physics motion demo. GOAL: a draggable card that snaps home with damped spring wobble, tuned live by stiffness and damping sliders. TECHNIQUE: the damped harmonic oscillator integrated per frame — acceleration = −k * position − c * velocity, then semi-implicit Euler: vel += acc*dt; pos += vel*dt with dt clamped to 0.032s, run in a requestAnimationFrame loop and written to el.style.transform as translate(px, px). While dragging, bypass the integrator and track the pointer directly (setPointerCapture + pointermove); on release, let the spring pull the card back to origin — overshoot and settle count are governed by k (stiffness 20-400) and c (damping 4-40), with underdamped tuning wobbling and overdamped tuning crawling. BUILD: (1) dark #0d0d0d stage with a 180px gradient card and a control panel; (2) two sliders with a monospace k/c readout; (3) a small tilt: rotate proportional to horizontal velocity while dragging for tactile feel. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no API keys, no libraries — hand-roll the physics, do not use a spring library. Cancel the rAF only if the page unloads. Under 140 lines.

TECHNIQUE: FLIP — First: record the source rect with getBoundingClientRect(); Last: reveal the destination element and record its rect; Invert: apply transform:translate(dx,dy) scale(sx,sy) mapping destination back onto the source (transform-origin:top left, dx = a.left − b.left, sx = a.width/b.width); Play: force a reflow with getBoundingClientRect(), then set transition:'transform 0.55s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)' and clear the transform so it animates to identity. Disable other transitions on the morphing element during the flip. BUILD: (1) dark #0d0d0d page with a 6-thumb picsum grid (ids 1015-1025) and a fixed full-screen detail overlay containing a large img and meta text; (2) click a thumb: copy its src into the detail img, unhide the overlay, and FLIP the img from the thumb's rect on the next frame; (3) clicking the overlay hides it (reverse morph optional). CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no API keys — hand-roll FLIP, no GSAP Flip. Under 150 lines.

name: Staggered Orchestration

why_pro: Turns static lists into choreographed reveals that read as premium.
demo_idea: A bento of tiles that cascade in with diagonal stagger on load, with a slider controlling the stagger amount live.

name: Inertial Smooth Scrolling
one_line: Lerp-smoothed scroll translation for weighted, eased wheel motion.
why_pro: The luxe scroll feel of award sites (Lenis-style).

name: Seamless Marquee Loops

Drive speed in a rAF loop: baseRate (0.6px/frame) plus a scroll-velocity boost (per-frame wheel delta, decayed *0.94 each frame, clamped ±14) — negative scroll reverses direction. Second band runs the same math negated for counter-motion. name: Text Scramble / Decode Effect

CONSTRAINTS: self-contained single HTML file, no build step, no virtualization library — implement it from scratch so the mechanism is visible. name: Optimistic UI Updates

why_pro: Screen-reader and keyboard users must never be stranded by a modal.

agent_prompt: You are building a fluid-simulation demo. GOAL: a full-screen ink pool the cursor stirs, with dye advection and splat presets. TECHNIQUE: simplified stable-fluids — grid arrays for velocity u/v and dye; each step: semi-Lagrangian advection (sample the dye field backwards along velocity: source = pos - vel·dt with bilinear-ish clamping), neighbor averaging for velocity diffusion, and Gaussian splats that inject velocity + dye color on interaction. For self-containment render the dye field via THREE.DataTexture updated each frame (set needsUpdate) on a fullscreen quad — production quality would use ping-pong framebuffers on the GPU, which you note in a comment. Drill-down re-runs the treemap scoped to the clicked node and re-maps scales: `x.domain([node.x0, node.x1]).range([0, W])` so children of any depth fill the viewport. BUILD: (1) Define a nested file tree (folders with children, files with byte sizes). (2) Render leaf cells as rounded rects colored by depth, labeled name + formatted size. name: Word/Tag Clouds & Packed Layouts
one_line: Frequency-typed labels packed without overlap (spiral placement).
why_pro: Text-heavy datasets summarized in one glyph-rich visual.
demo_idea: A tag cloud of a fake blog archive that re-packs on resize and filters by year slider, words flying to new spots.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a blog-archive tag cloud where word size encodes post count, tags re-pack without overlap on resize, and a year slider filters tags with words flying to their new positions.
TECHNIQUE: Archimedean spiral placement — for each tag, walk outward along `x = cx + cos(a)*r, y = cy + sin(a)*r*0.6` (angle increasing ~0.35 rad, radius ~1.6px per step), testing each candidate box against already-placed rects with axis-aligned overlap checks; the first non-colliding spot wins. Sizing: `fontSize = min + (count/max)*(max-min)`, and estimated width `text.length * fontSize * 0.62`. Positioning tags absolutely with CSS transitions on left/top/font-size gives the flying animation for free.
BUILD: (1) Define ~12 tags with total and per-year post counts. (2) Create absolutely-positioned span tags inside a bounded container. (3) Implement pack() with spiral placement and collision rejection. (4) layout(year) recomputes sizes and active states (count 0 → opacity .12), re-packs, and lets CSS transition the movement. (5) Wire the year slider, an "all years" reset, and re-pack on window resize.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Bound the spiral search so layout always terminates; keep transitions interruptible; keyboard-accessible tags (button elements or tabindex).

name: WebGPU-accelerated Inference
one_line: GPU compute paths for model execution in the browser.
why_pro: Real-time AI (segmentation, generation) needs GPU throughput.
demo_idea: A background-blur webcam demo that reports FPS with WebGPU enabled vs WASM fallback.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a benchmark page comparing a WebGPU compute path against a CPU (WASM-like) baseline on identical matrix-multiply workloads, with FPS-style reporting and a simulated backdrop-blur preview.
TECHNIQUE: WebGPU compute. `const adapter = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter(); const device = await adapter.requestDevice();` then a WGSL compute shader with `@compute @workgroup_size(8,8)` where each invocation computes one output cell of C = A×B from storage buffers. Pipeline: createShaderModule → createComputePipeline({layout:'auto'}) → createBindGroup → command encoder with beginComputePass/dispatchWorkgroups(SIZE/8, SIZE/8)/end → submit, timing with `await device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()`.
BUILD: (1) Add a Run benchmark button and a results table. (2) Time a naive JS matmul (CPU/WASM-like baseline), reporting ms and estimated GFLOP/s. (3) Feature-detect `'gpu' in navigator`; if present, build the pipeline and average 5 timed GPU dispatches into the table. (4) Add a button rendering a simulated person-mask blur preview to canvas, labeled with which path would run it.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Handle WebGPU absence and adapter/device rejection with visible fallback rows — the CPU path must always work; keep WGSL inline in a template literal.

name: Face & Landmark Detection

BUILD: (1) Stack a canvas over the <video> element. (2) Enable camera with getUserMedia, handling denial inline. (3) Load and initialize FaceMesh; draw a mesh subset (sampled landmark links + eye-region pairs) scaled to the canvas size. (4) Compute the iris center each frame and render a trailing cursor dot. (5) Show loading/ready status text throughout.

name: Pose Estimation
one_line: Skeleton keypoints from video feed, with confidence scores.
why_pro: Motion-controlled experiences and fitness apps in-browser.

agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a webcam "keepy-uppy" game where skeleton hand keypoints bounce a physics ball, with a keypoint overlay and live score.

Game loop is decoupled: gravity `vy += 0.25` every frame; a bounce triggers when the ball center is within `ball.r + 34` of a wrist while falling.
BUILD: (1) Stack an overlay canvas on the video; show a score readout. (2) Camera + model init behind a start button, with status/error text. (3) On each result: draw the skeleton bones array and key joints, then run ball physics and wrist-collision bounces (scoring +1, floor touch −1). (4) Draw the ball with an inner accent circle. (5) Keep physics running even when no person is detected.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, MediaPipe Pose via CDN script tag, inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect getUserMedia and window.Pose with graceful fallback text; handle camera denial inline; clamp ball velocity so it never escapes.

name: Background Removal / Segmentation
one_line: Per-pixel person/object masks applied to live video or images.
why_pro: Virtual backgrounds without servers — a killer client-side feature.
demo_idea: A webcam page that replaces your background with an animated CSS scene in real time, with a mask-quality slider.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a webcam page that replaces the user's background with an animated scene in real time, with a mask-quality slider controlling edge sharpness.
TECHNIQUE: MediaPipe SelfieSegmentation via CDN. `seg.setOptions({modelSelection:1})` (landscape model), `seg.onResults(res => {res.segmentationMask, res.image})`, and `seg.send({image: videoEl})` in a rAF loop. Compositing is canvas 2D blend modes: draw the animated background, then `drawImage(mask)` and set `globalCompositeOperation = 'source-in'` before drawing `res.image` so the person appears only where the mask is white. The threshold slider maps to `ctx.filter = contrast(k)` on the mask draw, which sharpens the alpha edge.
BUILD: (1) Hidden <video> + visible canvas; camera behind a start button with inline errors. (2) onResults: paint a moving gradient + drifting bubbles background each frame. (3) Apply the mask, switch composite op, draw the camera image, restore the op. (4) Wire the 0.2–0.9 threshold slider to the mask contrast. (5) Status text for loading/ready.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, MediaPipe via CDN script tag, inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect getUserMedia and window.SelfieSegmentation with graceful fallback text; the composite sequence must be exact or nothing renders — restore globalCompositeOperation every frame.

name: Object Detection Overlays
one_line: Bounding boxes + labels tracked over video in real time.
why_pro: AR-style informational UIs and smart cropping.
demo_idea: Point at household objects and get labeled boxes with confidence bars, drawn on a canvas over the feed.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a webcam object-detection overlay: labeled bounding boxes with confidence bars drawn on a canvas above the live feed, running fully on-device.
TECHNIQUE: TensorFlow.js + COCO-SSD via CDN scripts (`window.tf`, `window.cocoSsd`). `const model = await cocoSsd.load({base:'lite_mobilenet_v2'})`; each cycle `await model.detect(video, maxBoxes=8, minScore=0.45)` returns `[{bbox:[x,y,w,h], class, score}]` in video pixel coordinates — scale to canvas dims with sx = canvasW/videoWidth. Detection cadence: an async while-loop with a small setTimeout (~120ms) keeps the feed smooth.
BUILD: (1) Stack a transparent canvas over the <video>. (2) Start button: request camera, load the model with status text, begin the detect loop. (3) Per detection: clear, stroke a rounded-color box, draw a filled label chip (class + %), and a confidence bar under the box whose width = box width × score. (4) Cycle a color palette across detections.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, TF.js + coco-ssd via CDN script tags, inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect getUserMedia, window.tf, and window.cocoSsd with graceful fallback text naming what failed; handle camera denial inline; never block rendering while awaiting detect.

name: Streaming LLM Chat UI
one_line: Token-streamed text rendering with typing indicator and stop control.
why_pro: The chat UX pattern of the decade: perceived speed is everything.
demo_idea: A simulated chat where a fake model streams tokens with a cursor, stop button, and smooth markdown rendering.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a chat UI where a simulated model streams tokens into a bubble with a blinking cursor, a typing indicator before output, and a Stop button that aborts mid-stream.
TECHNIQUE: Token streaming is a paced loop: split the reply with `text.match(/\S+\s*|\n/g)` into word-ish tokens, then `for (const t of tokens){ await sleep(25 + Math.random()*45); }` inserting each token before a cursor element (`cursor.before(t)` keeps the cursor pinned at the end). Abort is a plain object `{stopped:false}` checked each iteration — in a real app this maps directly to AbortController. The typing indicator is a temporary bubble removed before streaming starts.
BUILD: (1) Chat log with user/bot message bubbles; auto-scroll to bottom on every append. (2) On send: push the user message, show a "thinking…" bubble for ~500ms, remove it, create the streaming bubble with a CSS blinking cursor span. (3) Stream tokens with randomized delay. (4) Stop button flips the abort flag, appends a "[stopped]" marker, hides itself. (5) Disable send while a stream is active.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Handle Enter-key submit; scrolling must not fight the user (always scroll during stream is acceptable here).

name: Incremental Markdown Rendering
one_line: Parse and render markdown as partial chunks arrive.
why_pro: Streamed answers must render formatted without flicker or layout jumps.
demo_idea: A 'model' streams a markdown answer (code blocks, tables, lists) that renders progressively with stable layout.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a page where a "model" streams a markdown answer (headings, lists, a table, a code block, a blockquote) that renders progressively with a cursor and never flickers or jumps layout.
TECHNIQUE: Incremental rendering via re-parse: keep the source as a token array (`md.match(/\S+\s*|\n/g)`), and on every tick call `out.innerHTML = marked.parse(partial) + cursorSpan` with the FULL partial so far — marked closes whatever blocks it can, so headings/tables/code appear as soon as their syntax is complete. Stream pacing is setInterval with variable chunk size (1–3 tokens per tick). Cursor is a CSS `@keyframes blink` inline-block span appended after the parsed HTML.
BUILD: (1) Include marked from CDN and setOptions({gfm:true, breaks:true}). (2) Write a rich markdown sample as a template literal. (3) Implement stream(): reset, renderPartial each 45ms, finalize with a full parse when tokens run out. (4) Add Replay and Show-final buttons (final clears the timer and renders everything). (5) Style pre/code/table dark so the answer looks native to the page.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, marked via CDN, inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect `window.marked` and fall back to streaming raw text with a note; avoid layout shift by never re-rendering a different container structure for the same prefix.

name: Client-side Embeddings & Semantic Search
one_line: Embed texts locally, cosine-rank query against vectors.
why_pro: Private RAG-ish search with no data leaving the device.
demo_idea: A notes app where search ranks by meaning not keywords — a matched-note similarity bar shown per result.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a notes app where search ranks by meaning rather than keywords, showing a similarity bar per result — all embeddings computed locally.
TECHNIQUE: transformers.js feature-extraction. `const extractor = await pipeline('feature-extraction', 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')`; embed with `extractor(texts, {pooling:'mean', normalize:true}).tolist()` to get one L2-normalized vector per string. Ranking is plain cosine similarity: `dot(a,b)/(‖a‖·‖b‖)` — with normalized vectors it's just the dot product. Query time: embed the query once, sort notes by score.
BUILD: (1) Define six notes where relevant pairs share NO keywords (e.g. query "how to keep my drink cold" should surface the insulated-bottle and cold-brew notes). (2) On load, build the pipeline, embed all notes, and store vectors. (3) On input (debounced or per keystroke), embed the query and re-render ranked results with a green similarity bar and percentage. (4) Empty query → neutral list order.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, transformers.js via CDN, inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect the library/model load and fall back to listing notes unranked with an explanatory status line; never block the page while the model downloads.

name: Generative Image Pipelines (client)
one_line: Diffusion or upscaling pipelines executed (or simulated) client-side.
why_pro: On-device generation is the frontier of private creative tools.
demo_idea: A 'latent journey' visual: interpolate noise into a stylized image with a progress tray of denoise steps.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a "latent journey" visualization that walks pure noise through a simulated denoising trajectory into a stylized image, with a progress tray of denoise steps you can click to revisit.
TECHNIQUE: The diffusion look comes from a schedule-driven neighborhood smoothing: each step replaces every pixel with a distance-weighted 3×3 average whose center weight shrinks as the schedule `strength = 0.28 + step*0.05` ramps — high-frequency noise decays first, exactly like diffusion's noise schedule. A seeded PRNG (mulberry32) makes runs reproducible; re-tinting channels with `putImageData` and time-varying sinusoids gives the stylized "latent" color grade.
BUILD: (1) Canvas at 128×128 latent resolution upscaled 2× with image-rendering:pixelated. (2) noiseImage(seed) fills a Float32Array with seeded uniform noise. (3) Generate: loop 12 steps via requestAnimationFrame — smooth, paint, snapshot the frame into a 72px tray thumbnail, and push the latent data for revisits. (4) Tray thumbnails are clickable, repainting their stored step. (5) Seed input regenerates deterministically.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Keep each step under ~16ms (128×128 is small enough); the tray must not grow unbounded; degrade gracefully without canvas support.

name: AI-assisted Content Utilities
one_line: Inline summarization, tone rewrite, and smart-crop suggestions.
why_pro: AI that appears as helpful micro-features, not chatbots.
demo_idea: A textarea with an 'improve' button that streams a rewritten version with a diff highlight between the two.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a textarea with a "✨ Improve" button that streams a tone-rewritten version of the text, then shows a word-level diff highlight between the original and the rewrite.
TECHNIQUE: Simulated local model (swap in transformers.js summarizer/paraphrase later — the UI contract is identical): stream tokens with `text.match(/\S+\s*|\n/g)` and a paced `await sleep(30–70ms)` loop inserting before a blinking cursor span. The diff is a classic word-level LCS: build `dp[i][j] = a[i]==b[j] ? dp[i+1][j+1]+1 : max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1])` (case-insensitive), then walk it forward emitting `<span class="del">` for original-only words, `<span class="add">` for rewrite-only words.
BUILD: (1) Source textarea pre-filled with an informal message. (2) Tone <select> (professional/friendly/concise) and the wand button. (3) On click: stream the rewrite with a cursor, then compute the LCS diff and replace the bubble with colored spans (green additions, struck-through red removals). (4) Status line explains the color code; disable the button during streaming.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Handle empty input inline; keep streaming interrupt-safe (button disabled); the diff must be computed only after streaming completes.

name: View Transitions (cross-document)
one_line: MPA navigations animated with the same morph primitives as SPAs.
why_pro: Server-rendered sites get app-grade transitions with @view-transition.
demo_idea: A two-page site where the shared logo and hero image morph seamlessly across a real page navigation.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a two-state site where the shared logo and hero image morph seamlessly across a real page navigation using cross-document View Transitions.
TECHNIQUE: Opt the whole document in with `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` at the top of the CSS on BOTH pages. Any element that should morph gets a unique `view-transition-name` (e.g. `.logo{view-transition-name:logo}`, `.hero{view-transition-name:hero}`) — matching names on the outgoing and incoming documents pair up automatically. Customize with `::view-transition-old(root), ::view-transition-new(root){animation-duration:.45s}`. Same-document fallback uses `document.startViewTransition(() => updateFn())`.
BUILD: (1) Build page one: header with a gradient logo tile + hero banner, nav link to a detail state. (2) Build page two with the same-named elements in new positions/sizes. (3) Add @view-transition and matching names to both. (4) Implement the same-document fallback path via startViewTransition for file:// contexts. (5) Add graceful degradation: if the API is unsupported, navigate instantly with no animation.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file per state (or one file handling ?page=detail), inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Never break navigation when View Transitions are missing — feature-detect and fall back.

name: Popover API
one_line: Declarative popovers with light-dismiss and top-layer positioning.
why_pro: Menus/toasts without z-index wars or focus-trap bugs.
demo_idea: A notification tray and menu set built purely on popover=auto with anchor positioning — one button toggles everything.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a notification tray and an action menu using only the Popover API — declarative attributes for opening/closing, native light-dismiss and Esc handling, no z-index management.
TECHNIQUE: Give a container `popover="auto"` and an id; open it from any button with `popovertarget="id"`. `auto` popovers close other popovers when opened, dismiss on outside click and Esc, and render in the top layer (no z-index wars). Close programmatically or declaratively with `popovertargetaction="hide"` on a button inside the popover. Style via the `[popover]` selector and `::backdrop`.
BUILD: (1) Three trigger buttons: Notifications, Actions menu, and an explainer. (2) Tray popover with a small notification list; menu popover whose items are buttons that self-close via popovertargetaction="hide". (3) Explainer popover demonstrating auto-exclusivity (opening one closes another). (4) Dark-theme [popover] and ::backdrop with border-radius and shadow. (5) Add a toggle listener that console.logs open/close state as a proof they're native events.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and minimal script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect `HTMLElement.prototype.hasOwnProperty('popover')` and show fallback text (or basic <details> fallback) in browsers without support.

name: <dialog> Element
one_line: Native modal/non-modal dialogs with ::backdrop and focus handling.
why_pro: Accessible modals with built-in top-layer and focus behavior.
demo_idea: A settings flow using nested <dialog>s with backdrop blur, Escape handling, and form method='dialog' return values.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a two-step settings flow using nested native <dialog> elements with backdrop blur, Escape handling, and form method="dialog" return values.
TECHNIQUE: `dialog.showModal()` opens a modal with native focus trapping and top-layer stacking; a second showModal() on top makes Esc close only the topmost dialog. Each dialog contains `<form method="dialog">` where the submitting button's `value` becomes `dialog.returnValue`, read in the `close` event. `dialog::backdrop` accepts backdrop-filter blur. `new FormData(form)` recovers field values before close.
BUILD: (1) Step-1 dialog: workspace name input + timezone select, Cancel and Next buttons (values "cancel"/"next"). (2) In the close handler, if returnValue is "next", build a summary from FormData and showModal() step 2. (3) Step-2 dialog: confirm/cancel buttons; its close handler reports the outcome. (4) Style both with ::backdrop blur and dark theming. (5) Demonstrate nested stacking so Esc peels dialogs one at a time.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect `HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal` and fall back to a simple inline panel if missing; form validation (required) must still gate submission.

name: <details>/<summary> Disclosures
one_line: Zero-JS disclosure widgets with animation via interpolate-size.
why_pro: FAQs, tree views, and menus without script or ARIA bookkeeping.
demo_idea: An animated FAQ accordion where name=group exclusivity and height auto-animation come purely from details attributes.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build an FAQ accordion that is 100% HTML+CSS: exclusive open/close via the details name attribute and smooth height animation via interpolate-size — no JS logic for the widget itself.
TECHNIQUE: `<details name="faq">` — sharing a name across multiple details elements makes the browser close the others when one opens (native exclusivity with correct semantics). Animation: wrap content in a .body div with `height:0; overflow:hidden; transition:height .3s`, add `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` on details so `details[open] .body{height:auto}` transitions smoothly. Decorate the marker with `summary::after{content:'+'; transition:rotate}` rotating to 45° when open.
BUILD: (1) Four FAQ items sharing name="faq", one initially open. (2) Style summaries with custom markers and hover states; hide the default ::-webkit-details-marker. (3) Add the .body height transition and interpolate-size declaration. (4) Feature-detect with CSS.supports('interpolate-size','allow-keywords') and print a status notice. (5) Verify clicking a second item closes the first with no script.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style, script used only for the feature-detect notice, no libraries, no build step, no keys. The widget must remain fully functional (open/close/exclusive) even when the animation feature is absent.

name: Custom Elements (Web Components)
one_line: Self-defined HTML tags with lifecycle callbacks and attributes.
why_pro: Framework-free reusable widgets that survive framework churn.
demo_idea: A <stat-counter> and <theme-toggle> custom element pair used across a page, inspectable in devtools as real tags.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a page using a <stat-counter> and <theme-toggle> custom element pair as real, reusable tags — inspectable in devtools, driven by attributes and lifecycle callbacks.
TECHNIQUE: `customElements.define('stat-counter', Class extends HTMLElement)`. The class uses `static observedAttributes = ['value','trend','label']`, `attributeChangedCallback()` to re-render, `connectedCallback()` for first paint and event wiring, and a shadow root for encapsulated styles. Reflecting state: getters/setters or attribute writes. Cross-element communication via bubbling CustomEvent dispatched on body.
BUILD: (1) Define stat-counter: shadow template with label/value/trend plus internal bump state incremented on click. (2) Define theme-toggle: a shadow button that flips document.body[data-theme] and dispatches a 'theme-change' CustomEvent. (3) Use three <stat-counter> tags with different attributes and one <theme-toggle> in plain HTML. (4) Have counters re-render on theme-change. (5) Host CSS custom properties (--card/--fg) so the page theme bleeds through the shadow boundary.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline script defining both elements, no frameworks, no build step, no keys. The tags must degrade to readable content if the script fails (put text fallbacks inside the elements); use :host styles exclusively for the component's own look.

name: Shadow DOM & Declarative Shadow DOM
one_line: Encapsulated style roots, now server-renderable via shadowrootmode.
why_pro: True style isolation for design systems and embeds.
demo_idea: A widget embed (like a Youtube-style card) whose styles can't leak, rendered with declarative shadow DOM — view source to see it.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a video-card widget whose styles provably cannot leak or be leaked into, rendered with declarative Shadow DOM — visible in view-source with zero JavaScript for its rendering.
TECHNIQUE: `<template shadowrootmode="open">` as the first child of the custom host element — the browser attaches the shadow root during parsing, so the widget renders before any script runs. Inside: a <style> block using `:host` selectors; the host page's CSS cannot match inside except through inherited CSS custom properties (--card, --fg, --mut), and widget selectors cannot escape. Expose styling hooks with `part="play"` for ::part() targeting.
BUILD: (1) Write deliberately hostile page CSS (forced background, uppercase tiny text, square buttons). (2) Create the <video-widget> element with a declarative shadow template: thumbnail, title, description, and a play button, all self-styled. (3) Show that page styles bounce off while custom properties still theme it. (4) Add a minimal script only for click handling. (5) Add an explanatory note about the encapsulation boundary.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style, no build step, no keys. The widget must render correctly with JavaScript disabled (that's the point of declarative shadow DOM); verify in the demo that page CSS cannot restyle widget internals.

name: PWA Install & Offline-first
one_line: Manifests + service workers caching for app-like installability.
why_pro: Reliable, installable web apps — the web's answer to app stores.
demo_idea: A note app that installs (manifest), keeps working offline (SW cache), and shows an install prompt with a status dashboard.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a note app that is installable as a PWA, keeps working offline via a service worker cache, surfaces an install prompt, and shows a status dashboard proving each capability.
TECHNIQUE: Three parts. (1) Manifest: build the JSON in JS and inject it as a Blob object URL <link rel="manifest"> so the demo stays single-file (name, display:'standalone', theme colors, data-URL icon). (2) Service worker: construct the SW script as a Blob and `navigator.serviceWorker.register(url)`; inside, `install` → caches.open + cache.addAll(shell), `fetch` → cache-first respond with network fallback, `skipWaiting`/`clients.claim()` for fast activation. (3) Installability: listen for `beforeinstallprompt`, preventDefault, stash the event, and call `.prompt()` from a button.
BUILD: (1) Note form saving to localStorage with a saved-confirmation status line. (2) Status dashboard listing SW state, install-prompt availability, and online/offline events. (3) Install button that only appears when beforeinstallprompt fired. (4) Test path: load once, go offline, reload — the shell and notes survive.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect serviceWorker and require http(s) — on file:// show a graceful explanation; never let a failed registration break the notes.

name: Service Worker Caching Strategies
one_line: Cache-first, network-first, stale-while-revalidate per route.
why_pro: Perf and resilience engineered at the network layer.
demo_idea: A 'cache lab' panel toggling strategies per asset type, with a request log showing hits from SW vs network (throttled).
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a "cache lab" where the user picks a caching strategy per asset class, fires test requests, and watches a live log distinguishing SW hits from network misses.
TECHNIQUE: Service worker fetch handler with pluggable strategies. The SW keeps a CONFIG object updated via `client.postMessage({type:'config', value})` / message listener. Strategies: cache-first (match cache, else fetch+put), network-first (try fetch, cache success, fall back to cache on failure), stale-while-revalidate (return cached hit immediately AND fire a background fetch to refresh). The SW logs each outcome back to clients via postMessage; the page renders it with color coding.
BUILD: (1) Two-column layout: strategy selects (static/api/images) + request log. (2) Blob-registered SW implementing all three strategies parameterized by asset kind (route classification by URL pattern). (3) pushConfig() sends changes; the SW confirms. (4) Fire button requests a mixed set of assets with cache-busting; log entries show "SW cache HIT", "network MISS → cached", "stale HIT (revalidating)". (5) Guard for non-SW contexts.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, SW injected as a Blob (no separate file), no build step, no keys. Must degrade with a clear notice on file://; log must be capped to avoid unbounded DOM growth.

name: WebTransport & WebSockets Streams
one_line: Low-latency bidirectional streams over HTTP/3.
why_pro: Real-time games and collaboration beyond WebSocket limits.
demo_idea: A shared cursor/whiteboard demo (simulated transport) showing latency graph comparison: WS vs WebTransport streams.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a shared-cursor whiteboard demo (simulated transport) with a latency graph comparing WebSocket-style framing against WebTransport-style datagrams, making the head-of-line-blocking difference visible.
TECHNIQUE: Abstract the transport into one function whose two modes differ only in delivery semantics: WS mode batches ALL pending cursor updates into one message per 60ms tick (later inputs wait for the whole batch — measure latency as tick-time + queue depth), WT mode delivers each update as an independent datagram with 4–8ms jitter and no queueing. Track rolling latency arrays per mode, draw them as two colored time-series on a canvas. Real WebTransport (`new WebTransport(url)`, `datagrams.writable`) is the upgrade path — feature-detect and note it.
BUILD: (1) Whiteboard board div with two cursor peers; local pointer drives peer A instantly, peer B follows via the simulated network. (2) Mode toggle buttons restyling the active one. (3) 60ms simulation tick applying the current mode's delivery model. (4) Canvas latency graph with gridlines, both series, and 100-sample window. (5) Stats line with rolling averages per mode.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. No real network calls — everything simulated; label it clearly as simulated; keep the tick loop stable.

name: WebHID / WebSerial / Web Bluetooth
one_line: Talk to hardware: gamepads, microcontrollers, IoT devices.
why_pro: Web as universal hardware dashboard — niche but magical demos.
demo_idea: A virtual 'device console' that connects to a simulated Arduino-like device over WebSerial, blinking an on-screen LED and charting sensor data.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a virtual "device console" that talks to an Arduino-like device — real WebSerial when available, a fully simulated device otherwise — blinking an on-screen LED and charting sensor readings.
TECHNIQUE: WebSerial: `'serial' in navigator` → `port = await navigator.serial.requestPort()` (user gesture required), `await port.open({baudRate:9600})`, then `port.writable.getWriter()` and `writer.write(new TextEncoder().encode('CMD\n'))`. The simulated device implements the same two-command protocol (LED_TOGGLE, READ) with a 40ms echo delay, toggling an LED div and returning a sine+noise temperature. The write path is one `writeLine(s)` function that routes to the real port or the simulator — identical app logic either way.
BUILD: (1) Device panel with an LED div (glow via box-shadow) and connection status. (2) Console pane with color-coded tx/rx/system lines. (3) Canvas temperature chart with rolling history. (4) Connect button tries real WebSerial, gracefully falls back to the simulator on refusal/absence. (5) LED toggle, single read, and a 400ms auto-stream toggle. (6) Disconnect cleanly (release writer, close port).
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Never throw if requestPort is denied — fall back and say so; cap console lines.

name: Gamepad API
one_line: Controller input with haptics for web games and interfaces.
why_pro: Console-grade input in browser experiences.
demo_idea: A racing mini-game drivable by a plugged-in controller, with an on-screen gamepad visualization and rumble on crash.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a tiny top-down racing game drivable by a plugged-in controller, with an on-screen gamepad visualization and rumble feedback on crashes.
TECHNIQUE: Gamepad API. Poll inside the rAF loop: `const g = navigator.getGamepads().find(g => g?.connected)`. Inputs: `g.axes[0]` steering with a ±0.12 deadzone, `g.buttons[7].value` (RT) throttle, `g.buttons[6].value` (LT) brake, `g.buttons[0].pressed` (A) boost. Haptics: `g.vibrationActuator.playEffect('dual-rumble', {duration, strongMagnitude, weakMagnitude})`. Connection lifecycle via `gamepadconnected`/`gamepaddisconnected` events. Keyboard (arrows/WASD) mirrors the same input variables as a fallback.
BUILD: (1) Canvas game loop: car with heading/velocity physics, obstacle circles, wall clamping. (2) Collision → velocity reversal, brief red flash, and a 220ms rumble scaled by impact speed. (3) HUD panel: stick knob translated by axes, A/B/LT/RT chips lighting when pressed, RT as a fill bar, gamepad id readout. (4) Wire keyboard fallback into the same steer/throttle/brake variables.
CONSTRAINTS: Self-contained single HTML file, inline style and script, no libraries, no build step, no keys. Never assume a pad exists — the game must be fully playable with keys; guard vibrationActuator with optional chaining; clamp velocity.

name: WebXR (VR/AR)
one_line: Immersive VR/AR sessions from the browser.
why_pro: Spatial web experiences without app installs.
demo_idea: A 3D gallery with an 'enter VR' flow (with emulator fallback) where panels float around the viewer, laser-pointer selectable.
agent_prompt:
GOAL: Build a 3D gallery with an "Enter VR" flow where panels float around the viewer and are laser-pointer selectable — with a desktop orbit fallback when no XR device exists.
TECHNIQUE: three.js WebXR. `renderer.xr.enabled = true`; capability detection via `navigator.xr.isSessionSupported('immersive-vr')`; session start with `navigator.xr.requestSession('immersive-vr', {optionalFeatures:['local-floor']})` then `renderer.xr.setSession(session)`. Rendering moves to `renderer.setAnimationLoop((t, frame) => …)` which XR takes over. Controllers come from `renderer.xr.getControllers()`; attach a laser line and raycast into panels for reticle placement. Desktop mode drives camera.rotation manually from pointer deltas.
BUILD: (1) Scene with 6 canvas-textured panels arranged in a circle around origin, gently bobbing. BUILD: (1) a paragraph and heading that select with a violet highlight; (2) a name input with violet caret, violet selection, and violet-tinted autofill background; (3) two toggle buttons — "Brand theme" and "Browser defaults" — swapping a body class that retargets all three custom properties at once; (4) log computed caret-color to the console as proof. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, inline styles/scripts, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect nothing; the -webkit-autofill rules simply no-op in Firefox. Dark neutral aesthetic (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4) with violet (#7c3aed) accent.

name: Console & Log-point Debugging

why_pro: Fast diagnosis beats fast guessing; pros instrument deliberately.
demo_idea: A demo page rendering styled console output (tables, groups, %c badges) triggered by interactions, opened next to the page.
agent_prompt: Build a demo page for Console & Log-point Debugging. name: Feature Detection & Progressive Enhancement
one_line: @supports, CSS.registerProperty guards, and baseline targeting.
why_pro: Ship cutting-edge CSS without breaking older browsers.
demo_idea: A component that upgrades itself (rounded → fancy anchor-positioned) as @supports checks pass, with a browser-capability panel.
agent_prompt: Build a self-upgrading component for Feature Detection & Progressive Enhancement. GOAL: identical markup renders at three capability tiers — solid base card, glassmorphism upgrade, anchor-positioned tooltip — and an on-page report lists exactly which checks passed in the current browser. TECHNIQUE: `@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(4px)) { … }` adds polish without removing base styles; `@supports (anchor-name: --a)` detects CSS anchor positioning; runtime checks use `CSS.supports('anchor-name','--a')` and `'IntersectionObserver' in window`; the tooltip positions via `position-anchor`/`position-area` when supported, else computes `getBoundingClientRect()` and uses fixed coordinates. BUILD: (1) a base card styled to work everywhere; (2) stacked `@supports` blocks that add backdrop-blur then anchor styling, each flipping the card's border color and stamping a ::before tier badge; (3) a monospace report panel running five checks (backdrop-filter, anchor-name, CSS.supports itself, IntersectionObserver, Popover API) with ✓/✗ lines; (4) a hover tooltip that uses whichever positioning path is available. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, inline styles/scripts, no build step, no keys. Rule: base tier must remain fully usable — enhancement never gates content. Dark neutral aesthetic (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4).

name: Print Stylesheets

BUILD: (1) a screen-styled dark article with a nav, a "no-print" paragraph, a callout box, and a chapter two section with sourced links; (2) a "🖨 Real print dialog" button calling `window.print()`; (3) a "👁 Simulated preview" button that renders a white, serif mock of the printed page including a dashed "— page break —" divider and URLs expanded after each link; (4) toggling the preview on/off. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, inline styles/scripts, no build step, no keys. Feature-detect nothing — @media print is universal. Screen view uses the dark neutral aesthetic (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4); print view is deliberately light.

name: Empty, Error & Loading State Craft

Dark neutral aesthetic (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4), blue primary CTA, muted supporting text.

name: Client Persistence Patterns
one_line: localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB for prefs, drafts, and queues.
why_pro: Drafts and preferences that survive reloads feel like respect.
demo_idea: A form with autosaving drafts, a storage inspector panel, and quota-failure handling shown in a status bar.
agent_prompt: Build a form with autosaving drafts, a storage inspector panel, and quota-failure handling. GOAL: typing triggers debounced persistence; a live inspector shows every key and byte usage; a "trigger quota failure" button demonstrates graceful degradation. TECHNIQUE: debounce input with `clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(save, 600)`; serialize state as `JSON.stringify({t, b, at: Date.now()})` under a namespaced key `draft:post`; estimate usage by summing `(localStorage[k].length + k.length) * 2` bytes against the ~5 MB quota; wrap `setItem` in try/catch for `QuotaExceededError` and fall back to an in-memory object. BUILD: (1) title input + monospace body textarea, both wired to the debounced autosave with an "edited… (saving in 600ms)" warning state then a green "autosave ✓ timestamp"; (2) restore the draft from localStorage on page load with a confirmation line; (3) a storage inspector sidebar listing each key (name, size, truncated value) plus a usage bar against 5 MB; (4) "Save now", "Clear drafts", and a red "💣 Trigger quota failure" button that writes two ~2 MB junk keys so the next autosave throws and the fallback path activates with an honest error message. CONSTRAINTS: single self-contained HTML file, inline styles/scripts, no build step, no keys. Dark neutral aesthetic (#0d0d0d, #e4e4e4).
